'''Robert Brown (Robby) Gardner''' ([[Tarrytown, New York]], February 27, 1939 – May 5, 1998) was an American [[mathematician]] who worked on [[differential geometry]].<ref name="remembering">{{citation
 | last = Wilkens | first = George R.
 | contribution = Remembering the mathematics of Robert Brown Gardner
 | contribution-url = http://www.math.hawaii.edu/~grw/Gardner/gardner.pdf
 | doi = 10.1090/pspum/064/1654541
 | location = Providence, RI
 | mr = 1654541
 | pages = 1–10
 | publisher = American Mathematical Society
 | series = Proceedings of Symposia in Pure Mathematics
 | title = Differential geometry and control (Boulder, CO, 1997)
 | volume = 64
 | year = 1999}}</ref> 

==Biography==
Gardner graduated from [[Princeton University]] in 1959,<ref name="unc">[https://math.unc.edu/in_memoriam/gardner-robert-brown-robby/ Robert Gardner, in memoriam]</ref> earned a master's degree from [[Columbia University]] in 1960,<ref name="cv">[https://math.unc.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/1318/2020/08/RBG_vitae.pdf Curriculum vitae of Robert Gardner]</ref> and completed his [[doctorate of philosophy|PhD]] in 1965 from the [[University of California, Berkeley]], under the supervision of [[Shiing-Shen Chern]].<ref name="gene">{{cite web |title=Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=http://www.genealogy.ams.org/id.php?id=22424 |accessdate=2015-06-29 |publisher=genealogy.ams.org}}</ref>

After this, he worked at many places, including the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], and worked as assistant professor at [[Columbia University]] between 1967 and 1970. He joined the faculty of the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] in 1971 and became a full professor there in 1977.<ref name="unc" /> He died on May 5, 1998.

== Research ==
Gardner was the author and co-author of three influential books, produced more than fifty papers,<ref>[http://www.unc.edu/math/Faculty/pbe/robbypapers.html Publications of Robert Gardner]</ref> eighteen masters students and thirteen Ph.D. students.<ref name="cv" /><ref name="unc" /> [[Robert Bryant (mathematician)|Robert Bryant]], [[Duke University]]'s Professor of Mathematics and the president of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (2015-2017) was a student of his.<ref name="gene" />

His 1991 book, ''Exterior Differential Systems'', coauthored with [[Robert Bryant (mathematician)|R. Bryant]],  [[Shiing-Shen Chern|S. S. Chern]], H. Goldschmidt, and [[Phillip Griffiths|P. Griffiths]], is the standard reference for the [[Exterior differential system|subject]].<ref name="remembering" />

He is better known in the United States for his improvements and popularization of the methods of [[Élie Cartan]] (most notably, [[Cartan's equivalence method]], an [[algorithm]]ic procedure for determining if two geometric shapes are different). The works of Cartan were hard to grasp for most students, and Gardner worked to explain them in more accessible ways.<ref>{{cite book |author=Fowler |first=Kristine K. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=i2mu7jg6OHEC&pg=PA184 |title=Using the Mathematics Literature |date=25 May 2004 |publisher=CRC Press |isbn=978-0-8247-5035-0 |page=184}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |author1=Marsden |first=Jerrold E. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lG4Gt_fyx4UC&pg=PA84 |title=The Breadth of Symplectic and Poisson Geometry: Festschrift in Honor of Alan Weinstein |author2=Ratiu |first2=Tudor |date=3 July 2007 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-0-8176-4419-2 |page=84 |author-link=Jerrold E. Marsden |author-link2=Tudor Ratiu}}</ref>

==Legacy==
In his memory, the UNC Mathematics Department created the Robert Brown Gardner Memorial Fund, devoted to supporting graduate student activities.<ref name="unc"/>

==Selected publications==
*''The Method of Equivalence and Its Applications'' {{ISBN|978-0-89871-240-7}}
*R. Bryant, S.-S. Chern, R. B. Gardner, H. Goldschmidt, P. Griffiths, ''Exterior Differential Systems'', [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|MSRI Publications]], Springer, 1990
*''Lectures on Exterior Algebras Over Commutative Rings''
*''Differential Geometric Methods in Partial Differential Equations''
